cases.sentence: ___, сделанная Алексеем Александровичем, представилась ему во всей своей силе.
cases.translation: The mistake made by Alexei Alexandrovich presented itself to him in all its force.
cases.explain: Ошибка is the grammatical subject of представилась (presented itself), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: он до этого дня не знал своего ___.
cases.translation: Until that day he had not known his own heart.
cases.explain: The negated verb не знал (did not know) governs the genitive case (genitive of negation).

cases.sentence: он сказал, прислушиваясь к ___ ребенка в соседней комнате.
cases.translation: He said, listening to the child's crying in the next room.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward, in response to) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Алексей Александрович подвинулся и хотел взять ее ___.
cases.translation: Alexei Alexandrovich moved closer and wanted to take her hand.
cases.explain: Руку is the direct object of the transitive verb взять (to take), so it is accusative.

cases.sentence: Алексей Александрович встал и с ___, ступая на цыпочки, подошел к ребенку.
cases.translation: Alexei Alexandrovich stood up and, walking on tiptoe with difficulty, approached the child.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) expressing manner governs the instrumental case, as in с трудом (with difficulty).

cases.sentence: В ___ февраля случилось, что новорожденная дочь Анны заболела.
cases.translation: At the end of February it happened that Anna's newborn daughter fell ill.
cases.explain: The preposition в (at/in) marking time governs the prepositional case, as in в конце (at the end).

reading.ru: Ошибка, сделанная Алексеем Александровичем в том, что он, готовясь на свидание с женой, не обдумал той случайности, что раскаяние ее будет искренно, и он простит, а она не умрет, эта ошибка через два месяца после его возвращения из Москвы представилась ему во всей своей силе.
reading.question: What mistake had Karenin made regarding his wife?
options: He had not considered that her repentance might be sincere and that she would not die
He had refused to visit her at all
He had told her he wanted a divorce immediately
reading.correct: He had not considered that her repentance might be sincere and that she would not die
reading.explain: The text says he had not thought through the possibility that her repentance would be sincere, he would forgive her, and she would not die.

reading.ru: Он у постели больной жены в первый раз в жизни отдался тому чувству умиленного сострадания, которое в нем вызывали страдания других людей, и которого он прежде стыдился как вредной слабости.
reading.question: What feeling did Karenin experience at his sick wife's bedside for the first time?
options: A feeling of tender compassion that he had previously been ashamed of as a harmful weakness
Anger and a desire for revenge
reading.correct: A feeling of tender compassion that he had previously been ashamed of as a harmful weakness
reading.explain: The text says he gave himself over to a feeling of tender compassion he had formerly been ashamed of as a harmful weakness.

reading.ru: Он простил жену и жалел ее за ее страдания и раскаяния.
reading.question: How did Karenin come to feel about his wife?
options: He forgave her and pitied her for her suffering and repentance
He demanded she leave the house
He refused to speak to her
reading.correct: He forgave her and pitied her for her suffering and repentance
reading.explain: The text states he forgave his wife and pitied her for her suffering and repentance.

reading.ru: Он простил Вронскому и жалел его, особенно после того, как до него дошли слухи об его отчаянном поступке.
reading.question: How did Karenin feel toward Vronsky after hearing about his desperate act?
options: He forgave him and pitied him
He challenged him to a duel
reading.correct: He forgave him and pitied him
reading.explain: The text says he forgave Vronsky and pitied him, especially after hearing rumors of his desperate act (the suicide attempt).

reading.ru: но к новорожденной маленькой девочке он испытывал какое-то особенное чувство не только жалости, но и нежности.
reading.question: What did Karenin feel toward the newborn baby girl, who was not his own daughter?
options: A special feeling of both pity and tenderness
reading.correct: A special feeling of both pity and tenderness
reading.explain: The text says he felt not only pity but also tenderness toward the newborn girl.

reading.ru: Он по нескольку раз в день ходил в детскую и подолгу сиживал там, так что кормилицы и няня, сперва робевшие пред ним, привыкли к нему.
reading.question: How often did Karenin visit the nursery, and how did the staff react over time?
options: He visited several times a day and sat long there; the wet-nurse and nanny, once timid, grew used to him
He visited once a week only
The staff remained afraid of him throughout
reading.correct: He visited several times a day and sat long there; the wet-nurse and nanny, once timid, grew used to him
reading.explain: The text says he went to the nursery several times a day and the wet-nurse and nanny, at first shy before him, grew accustomed to him.

reading.ru: Но чем более проходило времени, тем яснее он видел, что как неестественно теперь для него это положение, его не допустят оставаться в нем.
reading.question: What did Karenin come to realize as time passed?
options: That he would not be allowed to remain in his unnatural position
That his situation would improve on its own
That society fully approved of his arrangement
That Anna would soon recover completely and all would be forgotten
reading.correct: That he would not be allowed to remain in his unnatural position
reading.explain: The text says the longer time passed, the more clearly he saw he would not be allowed to remain in this unnatural position.

reading.ru: Когда прошло то размягчение, произведенное в ней близостью смерти, Алексей Александрович замечал, что Анна боялась его, тяготилась им и не могла смотреть ему прямо в глаза.
reading.question: How did Anna's attitude toward Karenin change once the softening effect of near-death had passed?
options: She feared him, felt burdened by him, and could not look him in the eye
She grew ever more affectionate toward him
She became completely indifferent to his presence
She began confiding all her secrets to him
reading.correct: She feared him, felt burdened by him, and could not look him in the eye
reading.explain: The text states Anna feared him, was burdened by him, and could not look him straight in the eyes.

reading.ru: В конце февраля случилось, что новорожденная дочь Анны, названная тоже Анной, заболела.
reading.question: What happened at the end of February?
options: Anna's newborn daughter, also named Anna, fell ill
reading.correct: Anna's newborn daughter, also named Anna, fell ill
reading.explain: The text says at the end of February the newborn daughter, also named Anna, fell ill.

reading.ru: «Кто здесь?» – спросил Алексей Александрович.
reading.question: What did Karenin ask upon entering the front hall?
reading.correct: "Who is here?"
reading.explain: Karenin asks «Кто здесь?» — 'Who is here?' upon seeing the footman.

reading.ru: «Княгиня Елизавета Федоровна Тверская».
reading.question: Who was the visitor announced to Karenin by the footman?
reading.correct: Princess Elizaveta Fyodorovna Tverskaya (Betsy)
reading.explain: The footman answers «Княгиня Елизавета Федоровна Тверская» — this is Princess Betsy Tverskaya.

reading.ru: Все как будто были в восторге, как будто выдавали кого-то замуж.
reading.question: How did the acquaintances around Karenin seem to behave during this difficult time?
options: As if they were all delighted, as though someone were being married off
As if they were mourning deeply
As if they were completely indifferent
As if they were angry with him
reading.correct: As if they were all delighted, as though someone were being married off
reading.explain: The text says everyone seemed to be delighted, as if someone were being given in marriage.

reading.ru: В первой детской Сережа, лежа грудью на столе и положив ноги на стул, рисовал что-то, весело приговаривая.
reading.question: What was Seryozha doing in the nursery when Karenin came in?
options: Lying on the table drawing something and cheerfully chattering
Reading a book with his governess
reading.correct: Lying on the table drawing something and cheerfully chattering
reading.explain: The text describes Seryozha lying with his chest on the table, feet on a chair, drawing and chattering cheerfully.

reading.ru: «Я думаю, что кормилица не годится, сударь», — решительно сказала англичанка.
reading.question: What did the English governess say about the wet-nurse?
options: That she thought the wet-nurse was not suitable
That the wet-nurse should be given a raise
That the wet-nurse was the baby's real mother
That the wet-nurse had already left
reading.correct: That she thought the wet-nurse was not suitable
reading.explain: The governess says decisively «Я думаю, что кормилица не годится, сударь» — she thinks the wet-nurse is not suitable.

reading.ru: Кормилица была без молока, сударь».
reading.question: What had happened in a similar earlier case cited by the governess, involving the wet-nurse?
reading.correct: The wet-nurse had no milk
reading.explain: The governess recalls that at Countess Pol's, the wet-nurse была без молока — had no milk.

reading.ru: «Несчастный ребенок!» — сказала няня, шикая на ребенка, и продолжала ходить.
reading.question: What did the nanny exclaim while trying to hush the crying baby?
reading.correct: "Poor child!"
reading.explain: The nanny says «Несчастный ребенок!» — 'Poor/unfortunate child!' while hushing her and continuing to walk.

reading.ru: Ему досадно было на жену за то, что она не заботилась об этом прелестном ребенке.
reading.question: Why was Karenin annoyed with his wife?
options: Because she was not taking care of the lovely baby
Because she had spent too much money
Because she refused to see Betsy
Because she had criticized his behavior
reading.correct: Because she was not taking care of the lovely baby
reading.explain: The text says he was annoyed with his wife because she was not looking after this lovely child.

reading.ru: «Если бы он не уезжал, я бы поняла ваш отказ и его тоже, но ваш муж должен быть выше этого», — говорила Бетси.
reading.question: What argument did Betsy make to Anna about Vronsky's request to say goodbye?
options: That if he weren't leaving, she'd understand the refusal, but her husband should be above such concerns
That Anna should never see Vronsky again
That Karenin had already agreed to the visit
That Vronsky no longer wished to see Anna
reading.correct: That if he weren't leaving, she'd understand the refusal, but her husband should be above such concerns
reading.explain: Betsy argues that if Vronsky weren't leaving she would understand the refusal, but Anna's husband ought to be above such pettiness.

reading.ru: «Я не для мужа, а для себя не хочу. Не говорите этого», — отвечал взволнованный голос Анны.
reading.question: Why did Anna say she did not want to see Vronsky?
options: For her own sake, not for her husband's sake
Because her husband had forbidden it
Because Vronsky no longer loved her
Because she was too ill to receive visitors
reading.correct: For her own sake, not for her husband's sake
reading.explain: Anna's agitated voice answers that it is not for her husband but for herself that she does not want it.

reading.ru: Анна в сером халате с коротко остриженными густой щеткой вылезающими черными волосами на круглой голове сидела на кушетке.
reading.question: How is Anna's appearance described when Karenin enters her room?
options: In a grey dressing gown, with her hair cropped short and growing out thickly, sitting on a couch
Dressed elegantly for a ball, standing by the window
Wrapped in furs, lying in bed asleep
reading.correct: In a grey dressing gown, with her hair cropped short and growing out thickly, sitting on a couch
reading.explain: The text describes Anna in a grey dressing gown with short, thickly growing black hair, sitting on the couch.

reading.ru: Вы удивительный муж», — сказала она с значительным и ласковым видом, как бы жалуя его орденом великодушия за его поступок с женой.
reading.question: How did Betsy praise Karenin when he entered?
options: She called him an amazing husband, as if awarding him a medal for magnanimity
She criticized him for neglecting his wife
She asked him to leave the room
reading.correct: She called him an amazing husband, as if awarding him a medal for magnanimity
reading.explain: Betsy says «Вы удивительный муж» in a meaningful, kindly tone, as if bestowing on him a medal of magnanimity.

reading.ru: «Но у вас как будто лихорадочный цвет лица», — сказал он, налегая на слово «лихорадочный».
reading.question: What did Karenin point out about Anna's complexion, with pointed emphasis?
options: That she seemed to have a feverish color, stressing the word "feverish"
That she looked pale and tired
That she looked much healthier than before
reading.correct: That she seemed to have a feverish color, stressing the word "feverish"
reading.explain: Karenin says her complexion looks feverish, deliberately stressing the word «лихорадочный».

reading.ru: Бетси говорила, что граф Вронский желал быть у нас, чтобы проститься пред своим отъездом в Ташкент.
reading.question: Why did Betsy say Vronsky wanted to visit?
options: To say goodbye before his departure for Tashkent
To ask Karenin's forgiveness in person
reading.correct: To say goodbye before his departure for Tashkent
reading.explain: Betsy explains that Vronsky wished to visit in order to say goodbye before leaving for Tashkent.

reading.ru: «Алексей Александрович, я знаю вас за истинно великодушного человека», — сказала Бетси, остановившись в маленькой гостиной и особенно крепко пожимая ему еще раз руку.
reading.question: How did Betsy address Karenin as she was leaving, while shaking his hand firmly?
options: She called him a truly magnanimous man
She thanked him for a gift
reading.correct: She called him a truly magnanimous man
reading.explain: Betsy tells him «я знаю вас за истинно великодушного человека» — 'I know you to be a truly magnanimous man,' while shaking his hand firmly.
